source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 19 June 1936, p. 13 ("Down County Council: Town Clerk of Newry Elected Vice-chairman"); Dromore Leader, 9 May 1936, p. 2 ("DOWN COUNTY COUNCIL."); Belfast News-Letter, 27 April 1933, p. 16 ("DOWN LOCAL ELECTIONS: Contests Likely For Four County Council Seats"); Newry Reporter, 20 June 1936, p. 3 ("Down County Council: Newry's Representative Elected Vice-Chairman")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: returned unopposed: 'There will be no contests for seats on Down County Council' and this division was not among the three changes (Dromore Leader, 9 May 1936, p. 2); sat as a member at the new council's first (annual) meeting on 18 June 1936 (Belfast News-Letter, 1936-06-19, p. 13: 'Mr. W. M. Cronin, town clerk of Newry, was elected vice-chairman') (meetings pass, 7 Nov 2026)

note: Triennial election of Down County Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1936 (Belfast News-Letter, 13 April 1936, p. 10). There were no contests. The Northern Whig of 9 May 1936 (p. 8) lists the twenty members who 'will comprise the new County Council', without divisions; each division is taken from the 1933 return or from the 1936 reports of the three changes (Bangor, Garvaghy, Portaferry: Belfast News-Letter, 7 May 1936, p. 15; Dromore Leader, 9 May 1936, p. 2) and Comber (J. M. Andrews's election notice, Northern Whig, 8 May 1936). No one was nominated for Dromore, where the retiring member, W. Liddell, was declared re-elected; he resigned and James Ervine was co-opted (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). division inferred from the 27 April 1933 return (W. M. Cronin, Newry); the Belfast News-Letter of 1936-06-19 names the member as sitting at the new council's first meeting. Returned unopposed.
